title: Const Volatile Pointer for Read-Only Hardware Timer
description:
One of the most famous embedded C interview questions is: *Can a pointer be declared both const and volatile at the same time?*

**Yes!** A read-only hardware status register or system timer register:
- It is `const` because firmware code must not write to it (read-only hardware).
- It is `volatile` because hardware alters it externally, so reads cannot be optimized away.

### Requirements:
1. `read_timer_count()`: Read from `TIMER_REG`.
2. `has_timer_expired()`: Unsigned subtraction `(current - start_tick) >= duration_ticks` which cleanly handles 32-bit integer overflow rollover.
hint: Unsigned arithmetic is defined modulo 2^N in C, meaning `current_tick - start_tick` correctly calculates elapsed time even across timer rollover.
